newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 sees no inflation pressure in Europe - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: G10 sees no inflation pressure in Europe - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the strength of the dollar had started to affect European import prices, but there were no signs of an inflationary environment.

"All in all, inflation is still under control," he told reporters at the Bank for International Settlements after a meeting of G10 central bank governors. Tietmeyer is chairman of the G10 central bank governors committee.
G10 governors also discussed foreign exchange markets at their monthly meeting, but Tietmeyer said the market seemed "relatively quiet".
"In Europe we see some effects on the import price side of the strength of the dollar in the last months," Tietmeyer said.
The impact on import prices varies from country to country, depending on the openness of the economies to international trade, he said.
"All in all, it is not the case that there is a new inflationary environment in Europe," he said, adding: "Monetary policy is more or less on the right track."
Tietmeyer cited Germany as an example of the effect the dollar was having on import prices.
"There is no strong likelihood of a spill-over effect on internal price developments," Tietmeyer said, noting that monetary policy still had to remain cautious.
Tietmeyer said the key issue and challenge for most continental European countries' policy makers was to try to reduce unemployment, but: "Monetary policy cannot solve the unemployment problem."
G10 central bankers also discussed the situation on financial markets, including equity and bond markets. In most countries, especially equity markets were on an upward trend, Tietmeyer said.
However, the only comment Tietmeyer made on financial markets was that monetary policy seemed to be on the "right track" in most countries.
However, in some countries some adjustment of monetary policy was probably necessary and debates are going on in those countries, he said. He declined to name them. -- Zurich newsroom +41 1 631 7340
